title: Predictive Throttling and Cache Coherence Playbook for Cross-Tenant Inference
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the predictive throttling and cache coherence strategy for cross-tenant inference traffic. It prescribes SLO-aware admission control, tenant CPU/GPU slot allocation, cache warming and invalidation primitives, instrumentation, and an operational runbook for diagnosing and mitigating tenant-induced QoS degradation. This is intended for teams operating Redwood-hosted clusters and Redwood Dedicated fleets; private deployments may adapt the policies but must maintain equivalent SLO guarantees.

Goals:
- Ensure 99.9% P95 latency SLO for latency-class A tenants under normal load.
- Limit cross-tenant cache pollution such that effective hit-rate loss < 5% for pinned-models.
- Bound tail-cost variance: no single tenant can increase cluster per-token cost by >10% in a 5-minute window.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to inference-serving runtime (service: inference-router, kv-coordinator, runtime-executor).
- Targets multi-tenant GPU pools (pool types: shared-gpu, reserved-gpu).
- Does NOT replace tenant-level quotas; supplements with adaptive, SLO-driven rules.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Predictive Throttling: A short-horizon controller that uses per-tenant request-rate forecasts and runtime signals (queue length, kernel utilization) to decide admission or redirection.
- Cache Affinity Window: Temporal window (default 60s) during which a tenant retains soft affinity to KV cache entries created by its requests.
- CPU/GPU Slotting: Lightweight allocation of fractional executor capacity for long-running streaming or stateful sessions.

SLOs and thresholds (default values):
| SLO/Metric | Target | Action threshold | Critical threshold |
|------------|--------|------------------|--------------------|
| P95 latency (latency-A) | <= 90ms | P95 > 120ms (5min) | P95 > 200ms (5min) |
| Cache effective hit-rate (pinned-models) | >= 85% | hit-rate drops 10% vs baseline | hit-rate drops 20% |
| Per-tenant 5-min cost delta | <= +10% | > +15% | > +25% (escalate) |

Architecture and control loop:
1) Signal collection: inference-router emits per-request telemetry (latency class, model-id, tenant-id, KV-touch-set). kv-coordinator reports cache occupancy and evictions per tenant. runtime-executor exports GPU utilization and kernel latency histograms.
2) Forecasting: short-window predictor (Holt-Winters with decay or lightweight ML predictor) estimates next 30–60s request volume per tenant.
3) Admission decision: controller computes tenant score = alpha * predicted_rate + beta * current_queue + gamma * cpu_utilization. If score exceeds pool threshold, controller will:
   - Deny best-effort requests (HTTP 429 with structured retry-after and cost_hint)
   - Redirect to cheaper model variant (if tenant policy permits)
   - Enforce slotting limit on streaming sessions (soft pause or scale-down)
4) Cache coherence actions: when tenant-induced eviction rate for pinned-models > eviction_threshold (default 0.12), controller reduces admission for offending tenants and triggers proactive prefetching for affected tenants.

Config sample (YAML - runtime controller):
controller:
  pool_check_interval: 2s
  predictive_horizon_seconds: 45
  tenant_score_weights:
    predicted_rate: 0.6
    queue_length: 0.25
    gpu_util: 0.15
  admission_action_order: [deny, redirect, slot_limit]
  eviction_threshold: 0.12
  cache_affinity_window_seconds: 60
  cost_delta_alert_pct: 15

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- Required metrics: tenant.p95_latency_ms, tenant.predicted_rps, tenant.queue_length, tenant.kv_eviction_rate, tenant.gpu_util_percent, tenant.cost_delta_pct.
- Required spans: /v1/generate entry and exit; kv-coordinator cache hit path with tenant-id tag.
- Dashboards: Tenant QoS dashboard (per-tenant heatmap), Pool health (aggregate tail latencies), Cache coherency panel (eviction rates by model/tenant).
- Alerts:
  - Alert THROTTLE_HIGH when >5% of tenants in a pool are in admission-deny state for >3m.
  - Alert CACHE_STRESS when pinned-model hit-rate drops >15% for >2m.

Operational runbook (triage steps):
1) Detect: Pager triggers for THROTTLE_HIGH or CACHE_STRESS.
2) Identify affected pool and tenants: use Tenant QoS dashboard -> filter by pool_id.
3) Gather evidence: export last 15m of tenant.* metrics and trace samples for top 5 tenants by predicted_rps.
4) Mitigate (fast path):
   - For runaway tenant (high predicted_rps + high evictions): temporarily apply hard quota (deny requests) and notify Customer Success.
   - For spike caused by model checkpoint change (increased KV footprint): trigger emergency cache prewarm for pinned-models and increase cache_affinity_window to 120s for impacted tenants.
   - For kernel-level saturation (GPU util ~ 100%): shift low-priority tenants to reserved-gpu-burst topology if configured.
5) Post-mortem: capture root cause (bug, user behavior, model change), performance impact (tokens, cost), and corrective actions. Update tenant-specific runbooks.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests: controller scoring logic, admission decision matrix, synthetic predictor inputs.
- Staging: run controller in observe-only mode for 2 weeks against shadow traffic. Evaluate false positive/negative rate for admission decisions.
- Canary: enable admission actions for 5% of traffic in a single pool; monitor THROTTLE_HIGH and SLO regressions for 48 hours.
- Gradual rollout: increase to 25% then 100% across pools, with automated rollback if P95 regressions exceed 10% above baseline.

Compatibility and integration notes:
- API contract: admission responses must follow structured error schema (application/json) with fields: code, message, retry_after_seconds, suggested_model_variant. See API standard: canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025 for format.
- SDKs should surface 429 with retry metadata to customers and include a client-side backoff that respects suggested retry_after.
- Private deployments: controller configuration defaults may be more conservative; ensure equivalent unit tests and telemetry hooks are installed.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owners: runtime-inference team (oncall rotation: runtime-inference@redwood.com).
- Secondary owners: infra-sre (capacity & node-level interventions), platform-telemetry (dashboard/alert maintenance).
- Escalation matrix:
  1) runtime-inference pager (P1)
  2) infra-sre lead (within 15 minutes)
  3) Eng director oncall if incident not contained within 1 hour

Open questions and decision notes (ADR candidates):
- ADR Candidate A: Standardize tenant score formula and weight calibration across pool shapes. Proposed owner: Miguel Santos.
- ADR Candidate B: Define canonical tenant cost attribution window (5m vs 15m) used by controller and billing systems. Proposed owner: Finance-legal to coordinate.

Appendix A — Example 429 payload (JSON):
{
  "code": "THROTTLED_TENANT",
  "message": "Traffic exceeds current pool capacity; retry after the suggested delay or use a lower-cost model variant.",
  "retry_after_seconds": 30,
  "suggested_model_variant": "model-123-quantized"
}

Appendix B — Simulation test matrix:
- Scenario 1: Single tenant ramp from 10 RPS -> 500 RPS in 60s. Expected outcome: predictor flags spike; admission reduces best-effort by 70% and redirects 30% to cheaper variants.
- Scenario 2: 20 tenants uniform ramp; expected outcome: pool-level smoothing kicks in; no single tenant enters deny state; tail latency within SLO.
- Scenario 3: Model rollout with new checkpoint increasing KV footprint by 3x; expected outcome: temporary hit-rate degradation; trigger prewarm and affinity window extension.
